_about: Hand-written comments for the course browser, merged in by build_browser.py. Summaries and key ideas are Claude's own wording, written from the transcribed slides. Papers are the paper-discussion readings listed on the course page (fetched 2026-10-04); titles ending in '...' were truncated there.

01.summary: Course logistics (paper discussions, four homeworks, group projects on SO-101 arms, 20/40/40 grading), then why robotics is hard: Shakey and sense-plan-act, robots falling when state estimation fails, Moravec's paradox. Ends with why now (cheap humanoid hardware, data scaling, foundation models) and the framing that runs through the whole course: robotics as multimodal sequence modeling.
key_ideas: Robot learning = solving robotics (perception, control) with machine learning (imitation, RL, representation learning)
Moravec's paradox: abstract thinking is easy for AI, sensorimotor skill is hard
A policy maps image + language instruction to an action; a VLM maps image + prompt to text - same shape of problem
Scaling needs three ingredients: large datasets, large models, scalable evaluation
Imitation learning assumes i.i.d. data; in RL actions change future states

02.summary: Classical robotics toolkit first: rigid-body transforms in SE(2)/SE(3), kinematic chains, degrees of freedom, configuration space vs workspace vs task space, forward and optimization-based inverse kinematics, smooth trajectories (LERP vs quintic splines) and PID tracking. Second half sets up decision making: policies, states vs observations, the Markov property and the MDP objective.
key_ideas: Chain transforms by multiplying homogeneous matrices: T_base_ped = T_base_sensor x T_sensor_ped
IK is non-unique; solve it by gradient descent with the Jacobian transpose
LERP gives velocity jumps and acceleration spikes; quintic time scaling starts and ends at rest
PID: P pulls toward the target, I fights steady offsets like gravity, D damps overshoot
MDP = (S, A, P, R); the objective is expected (discounted) return over trajectories

papers.title: Simple random search provides a competitive approach to reinforcement learning
Deep Reinforcement Learning Doesn't Work Yet

03.summary: Behavioral cloning and why it breaks: compounding errors from distribution shift (O(eps T^2)), fixed by side-camera augmentation, DAgger (O(eps T)) and human-gated interventions. Then non-Markovian experts and causal confusion, and multimodal demonstrations, handled by Gaussian mixtures, autoregressive discretization, diffusion and latent variable models. Closes with goal- and language-conditioned learning from play data.
key_ideas: BC is supervised learning on non-i.i.d. data: small errors push the robot off the expert's state distribution
DAgger relabels the states the policy actually visits with expert actions
Adding history can hurt: the policy may latch onto spurious cues (causal confusion)
MSE averages the modes of a multimodal expert - the skier hits the tree
Latent plans: a posterior encodes the demo, a prior proposes plans from start and goal, a KL term ties them

04.summary: Value-based RL from the ground up: sparse rewards are smooth in expectation, value functions and the Bellman equation, value iteration, policy evaluation and policy iteration (with live gridworld demos), Q-values, tabular Q-learning vs SARSA, then deep RL: DQN with replay and target networks, double DQN, and three ways to take an argmax over continuous actions (discretization, CEM as in QT-Opt, a learned actor as in DDPG).
key_ideas: Bootstrapping: V(s) = r + gamma V(s') lets you evaluate without full rollouts
Acting with V needs a dynamics model; acting with Q only needs an argmax
Q-learning is off-policy (max over next actions), SARSA on-policy (the action actually taken) - SARSA learns the safer cliff path
DQN stabilizers: replay buffer breaks correlations, frozen target network fixes the regression target
Max over noisy estimates overestimates; double DQN decouples selection and evaluation

papers.title: Evolution Strategies as a Scalable Alternative...

05.summary: Policy gradients: the log-derivative trick, REINFORCE, variance reduction with reward-to-go, baselines and the advantage function, off-policy updates via importance sampling, then the trust-region family (TRPO, PPO) and actor-critic methods ending with SAC and the reparameterization trick.
key_ideas: Policy gradient = imitation gradient weighted by return
Baselines do not bias the gradient; V(s) is the natural one, giving the advantage A = Q - V
Importance weights let you reuse old data but explode over long horizons
PPO clips the probability ratio instead of solving TRPO's KL-constrained problem
SAC trains the critic fully off-policy from a replay buffer - the most sample-efficient of the lot

papers.title: End-to-End Training of Deep Visuomotor Policies

06.summary: How to represent full action distributions: autoencoders, VAEs (ELBO, reparameterization), VQ-VAEs (codebook, straight-through estimator), diffusion (DDPM training and sampling, the closed-form noising shortcut, DDIM, classifier-free guidance) and flow matching / rectified flow, with robotics case studies: Diffusion Policy, DiT-Block Policy and pi0.
key_ideas: VAE latents are sampleable because the KL term pins them to N(0, I)
VQ-VAE swaps the Gaussian for a discrete codebook; a prior over code sequences generates new data
Diffusion trains a noise predictor; x_i can be sampled from x_0 in one step
DDIM is a deterministic, few-step version of DDPM sampling
Flow matching regresses a constant velocity from noise to data and integrates it with Euler steps

07.summary: Why robots need history, then the transformer stack: attention (with a live step-through), positional encodings, encoder-decoder vs decoder-only, teacher forcing, BPE tokenization, scaling laws. Extends to vision (ViT patches, CLIP, LLaVA early fusion, Flamingo late fusion, native multimodal models) and finally to actions: per-dimension binning (RT-2, OpenVLA), action chunking (ACT) and FAST compression.
key_ideas: Attention gives O(1) path length between any two tokens; RNNs need O(n)
Compute-optimal training: scale parameters and tokens together, ~20 tokens per parameter
VLMs differ mainly in where vision enters: prepended tokens, cross-attention, or joint training from scratch
Naive binning breaks at high control frequency - adjacent tokens become nearly identical
FAST = DCT + BPE on action chunks, like JPEG for actions

papers.title: Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling
Humanoid Locomotion as Next Token Prediction

08.summary: Starts with mid-term feedback and the five final-project briefs. Then world models P(s' | s, a, h): pixel-space models with visual MPC, latent models (Ha and Schmidhuber's V-M-C, the RSSM of PlaNet, Dreamer V1-V4), video tokenization and compression, video backbones for policies (mimic-video, DreamZero) and JEPA, which predicts in latent space with no decoder at all.
key_ideas: A world model is a learned simulator: actions in, future states out
RSSM keeps a deterministic memory h_t plus a stochastic z_t, and learns a prior so imagination does not drift
Dreamer trains the policy entirely in imagination by backprop through the frozen model
Video models already know physics from internet video, so policies on top need far less robot data
JEPA avoids pixel prediction; the risk is collapse, prevented by EMA targets, frozen encoders or Gaussian regularization

papers.title: Learning Universal Policies via Text-Guided Video...
Training Agents Inside Scalable World Models
World Action Models are Zero-shot Policies

09.summary: How to build a generalist policy: aggregate existing robot data (Open X-Embodiment), design for heterogeneous sensors and actions (Octo's tokenizers and readout tokens, CrossFormer across robots), start from internet-scale VLMs (VLAs), and evaluate cheaply in simulation that correlates with the real world (SIMPLER). Includes practical training tips: convergence metrics, batching mixed datasets, sequence packing, data loading.
key_ideas: Pooling 60 datasets from 34 labs beat each lab's own specialist method on average
Readout tokens let new action heads and observation types be attached at fine-tuning time
A VLA reuses the VLM's vocabulary for 256 action bins
Current recipe: next-token prediction on FAST actions + web data, plus a flow-matching action expert behind a stop-gradient
Real-to-sim evaluation works when control dynamics (SysID) and visuals are matched

papers.title: pi*0.6: a VLA That Learns From Experience

10.summary: Embodied chain-of-thought: VLAs that generate a plan, subtask, movement and grounded boxes before acting, trained on reasoning data generated by foundation models. Reasoning helps but costs ~4 s per action, so ECoT-Lite keeps the benefit with reasoning pre-training and reasoning dropout. Then test-time compute in Go and language, chain-of-thought, RL-trained reasoning (GRPO, DeepSeek-R1) and verifiers for visual reasoning.
key_ideas: Reasoning chains make policies interpretable and correctable by a human
Three explanations for why reasoning helps: better representations, a curriculum, more compute per action
Training on reasoning but dropping it at test time keeps most of the gain at full speed
Test-time search can substitute for huge model scale (AlphaGo Zero: ~100,000x)
GRPO needs no critic: rewards are normalized within a group of sampled answers

papers.title: Training Strategies for Efficient Embodied Reasoning

11.summary: A survey of what is still unsolved: hype vs real generalization, which backbone and data recipe to bet on, data collection interfaces, dexterity beyond vision (touch, audio), knowing when to reason or ask for help, scaling RL with a data flywheel, lifelong learning, rapid in-context adaptation, unified mobile manipulation and multimodal memory. Ends with advice on doing research and the lecturer's own PhD story.
key_ideas: Data scalability trades off against hardware alignment: egocentric video scales best, teleop matches the robot best
Adaptive test-time compute: react fast when certain, reason when uncertain, escalate when lost
Introspection - knowing what you don't know - is an open problem
Good research problem = important problem + plan + excitement + your own reviewer #2

papers.title: A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence
